findings.claim: Singapore's CPF contribution rate is 37 percent, worker and employer together, for workers aged 55 and under, on wages in the top band.
findings.evidence: S: data/cpf_contribution_rates.csv, the 2026-01 rows (lines 668-675): Employer 17 and Employee 20 for '35 years & below', 'Above 35 - 45', 'Above 45 - 50' and 'Above 50 - 55'. I summed them with a script and each group comes to 37.0. 'Above 55 - 60' (lines 676-677) comes to 16+18=34, so 'aged 55 and under' marks the edge correctly. 2026-01 is the last effective_from in the file, and the file was fetched 2026-10-21, so the present tense holds. The CSV sha256 c4529a8e... matches provenance-audit.md. Dataset description in meta_d_98ffa142ae0dec40391f78f81d26aca9.json (sha256 26daef4b... matches; name 'CPF contribution rates'; column 'contribution_rate'): 'As a proportion of wage ... The CPF contribution rates are applicable for the highest wage band.' So 'contribution rate' is the dataset's own term and 'top band' renders 'highest wage band'. results.json contributions.cpf: total_pct 37.0, max_age 55, in_force 2026-01. The site MDX:86 is identical to draft .md:52. Note, not a defect: the sector scope in the description ('private sector employees and public sector non-pensionable employees') is not in the sentence. That omission predates round 6 (round 2 item 7 confirmed the sentence), and 'worker and employer together' already implies employees. The sentence has no in-text citation, but Method notes (draft .md:85) cites Central Provident Fund Board, 2026 and the reference is at .md:119. | L: 'Contribution rate' is the source's own term. The dataset is named 'CPF contribution rates' and described 'As a proportion of wage ... The CPF contribution rates are applicable for the highest wage band. For example, the rates for January 2014 are applicable for wages of $750 or more per month' (sources/provenance/cpf/meta_d_98ffa142...json, data.name and data.description). In data/cpf_contribution_rates.csv the 2026-01 rows give Employer 17 + Employee 20 = 37 for '35 years & below', 'Above 35 - 45', 'Above 45 - 50' and 'Above 50 - 55'. 'Above 55 - 60' is 34 (computed in lens-L/logic_checks.txt). results.json contributions.cpf has total 37.0, max_age 55, in_force 2026-01. Under the rate framing the sentence states a rate, not a share of total pay. It stays true where the Ordinary Wage ceiling binds, because the ceiling limits the wage base, not the rate. This matches the owner decision of 2026-10-23. Old wording in 6.json, 'Singapore's CPF takes 37 percent of pay', is gone from the .md, .src.md, MDX:86 and .docx (I extracted the docx text). | H: Sentence at draft .md:52, .src.md:52 (bound to {{contributions.cpf.total_pct:int}} and {{contributions.cpf.max_age:int}}) and site MDX:86, all identical. Round 6's only change here was 'takes 37 percent of pay' to 'contribution rate is 37 percent'. Figure: data/cpf_contribution_rates.csv rows effective 2026-01 give Employee 20 and Employer 17 for all four age groups up to 'Above 50 - 55 years', and 'Above 55 - 60' drops to 18 and 16. results.json has contributions.cpf total_pct 37.0 and max_age 55. 'Top band': the stored metadata (sources/provenance/cpf/meta_d_98ffa142ae0dec40391f78f81d26aca9.json) says the rates 'are applicable for the highest wage band ... wages of $750 or more per month'. On the hostile CPF member's objection about the ceiling: I fetched the CPF Board's own rate table (cpf.gov.sg CPFcontributionratesfrom1Jan2026.pdf, 2026-10-23, saved to lens-H/dl/cpf_rates_2026.pdf, sha256 7ab21a34...). Table 1, row '55 & below', band '> $750', gives the rate as '[37% (OW)]* + 37% (AW)' with '* Max. of $2,960' and the note 'OW: Ordinary Wages (capped at OW ceiling of $8,000)'. So the Board itself states 37% as the contribution rate and treats the ceiling as a separate cap on the wage base. With the rate framing the sentence holds for every top-band employee aged 55 and under, including those paid above the ceiling. The old 'of pay' wording was false above S$8,000 (lens-H/cpf_ceiling_check.txt: 19.7% of S$15,000). Read alone, the sentence contains no contrast that implies CPF has no ceiling. The Indonesian and BPJS readers have nothing in it to object to. A US economist finds no comparison stated here.

findings.evidence:

(b) CPF: 37 for ages 55 and under on the top band, as in item 2 (results.json cpf.total_pct 37, max_age 55; meta 'highest wage band'). (e) JP '3 percent on wages up to a ceiling': PP 45/2015 Pasal 28(2), pp_45_2015.txt:824-825 ('3% (tiga persen) dari Upah per bulan'). Pasal 29(2), pp_45_2015.txt:855-858, which I re-extracted from the PDF itself (sha256 f48fe915... matches): 'Batas paling tinggi Upah yang digunakan sebagai dasar perhitungan Iuran Jaminan Pensiun untuk tahun 2015 ... Rp7.000.000,00'. Pasal 29(3), :859-864, indexes that cap each year. results.json jp.total_pct 3. The gate.toml:74 template renders to exactly the text at site MDX:78 and in 7.json. | L: The MDX:78 alt text is identical to the inventory text (script comparison: True), and it renders gate.toml:74. Clause by clause: (a) 'contribution rates each year, worker and employer' matches the chart title and its stacked bars. (b) CPF 37 percent, aged 55 and under, top band: see item 2. (c) '12.1 percent on average among participants in 2024': the HAS highlights row 'Average total contribution rate (participant and employer) ... 12.1%' in the 2024 column (vanguard_how_america_saves_2026.txt:224), and body text :2563-2566 says 'the average total participant contribution rate ... These rates exclude eligible nonparticipants'. (d) 'JHT, 5.7 percent': PP 46 Pasal 16(1) (pp_46_2015.txt:428-434). (e) 'JP, a separate pension, 3 percent on wages up to a ceiling': PP 45 Pasal 28(2) '3% ... dari Upah per bulan' (pp_45_2015.txt:822-823) and Pasal 29(2)-(3), the maximum wage base, Rp7,000,000 in 2015 and indexed yearly (:855-864). No clause gives JP or CPF as a flat share of pay. | H: Published alt text (gate.toml:74, rendered at site MDX:78). Comparing draft/.rounds/6.json with 7.json: the lead-in changed, and the JP clause went from '3 percent.' to '3 percent on wages up to a ceiling.' The CPF clause stayed '37 percent for workers aged 55 and under, on wages in the top band'. Before round 6 the alt text qualified neither rate. Now one sentence sets 'on wages in the top band' (CPF) against 'on wages up to a ceiling' (JP). The top band has no upper limit: the stored metadata gives 'wages of $750 or more per month', and CPF Table 1 gives '> $750'. Read alone, the alt text says JP stops at a ceiling and CPF's 37 percent covers the whole top band. CPF has a ceiling too. CPF Board Table 1 (fetched 2026-10-23, lens-H/dl/cpf_rates_2026.txt:5-42) says 'OW: Ordinary Wages (capped at OW ceiling of $8,000)' and '[37% (OW)]* ... * Max. of $2,960'. The CPF FAQ 'What is the Ordinary Wage (OW) ceiling?' says it is 'the maximum amount of OW that attracts CPF contributions in a calendar month', $8,000 from 1 January 2026. My computation (lens-H/cpf_ceiling_check.txt): S$2,960 is 19.7% of S$15,000 and 14.8% of S$20,000. So a Singaporean CPF member can quote the contrast as misleading for pay above S$8,000, and an undefined 'top band' that a lay reader takes to mean high earners makes this worse. This is the ground of r6:extra:H2 (REFUTED LOW, upheld by its skeptic). The owner's rate framing fixed H2's 'of pay' wording, but round 6 also added the JP-only qualifier inside this one sentence, which sharpens the contrast H2 described. The other clauses survive. 401(k): How America Saves 2026, Figure 44, 2024 column 'Average total contribution rate (participant and employer) ... 12.1%' (vanguard_how_america_saves_2026.txt:224), and 'These rates exclude eligible nonparticipants' (:2566-2569). The alt text labels it 'on average among participants', so the economist's objection that it is an average fails. JHT 5.7 percent with no qualifier is right: PP 46 Pasal 17 sets no ceiling (r6:item:1 (e)). JP '3 percent on wages up to a ceiling' matches PP 45 Pasal 28(2) and 29(2). The chart PNG (opened) matches the bar values. | skeptic H: My re-check supports the finding at LOW severity. The issue is the contrast inside one sentence, not any single number.

(1) Where the text is: gate.toml:74 and site MDX src/content/blog/forced-to-save-and-i-never-knew-it.mdx:78 both carry the quoted wording. In draft/.rounds/5.json and 6.json the alt text ends 'JP, a separate pension, 3 percent.' under the lead-in 'what goes in each year as a share of pay'. In 7.json the lead-in is 'contribution rates each year' and the JP clause is '3 percent on wages up to a ceiling'. The CPF clause is the same in all three. So round 6 added a ceiling qualifier to JP only.

(2) The two clauses have the same shape. CPF gets 'on wages in the top band' and JP gets 'on wages up to a ceiling', so each clause tells the reader which wages its rate applies to. The 'top band' has no upper limit. The stored metadata (sources/provenance/cpf/meta_d_98ffa142ae0dec40391f78f81d26aca9.json) says the rates 'are applicable for the highest wage band', for example 'wages of $750 or more per month'. Read side by side, the clauses imply CPF has no cap.

(3) CPF does have a cap. I ran pdftotext myself on lens-H/dl/cpf_rates_2026.pdf

findings.claim: JHT and JP: the rates the regulations set (PP 46/2015 Pasal 16; PP 45/2015 Pasal 28). 401(k): Vanguard, How America Saves 2026, plans Vanguard keeps records for, 2024, among participants: the average deferral rate as the worker share, and the average total contribution rate less that as the employer share (a difference of two averages). 401(k) deferrals are optional. CPF: CPF Board contribution ra
findings.evidence: S: 'JHT and JP: the rates the regulations set (PP 46/2015 Pasal 16; PP 45/2015 Pasal 28)': Pasal 16(1) sets 5.7% (2% worker, 3.7% employer; pp_46_2015.txt:428-434). Pasal 28(2)-(3) sets 3% (2% employer, 1% worker; pp_45_2015.txt:824-833). Both are Peraturan Pemerintah (government regulations), so 'regulations' is accurate. 'JP is a separate pension scheme, and its rate applies to wages up to a ceiling': Pasal 29(2) caps the wage used as the base for JP contributions (Rp7,000,000 a month in 2015; :855-858), and Pasal 29(3) has BPJS adjust that cap every year by 1 plus GDP growth (:859-864). The rate applies only up to the cap, so the sentence matches. provenance-audit.md section G, 'JP contribution: a wage ceiling', records the same reading. The 401(k) and CPF clauses are unchanged since round 6 and match the sources: HAS :214 and :224, 2024 values 7.6 and 12.1; CPF 2026-01 rows; meta 'highest wage band'. The text is the same in make_charts.py:171-177, the opened PNG and site MDX:79-83, and site public/images/blog/jh-3-contributions.png is byte-identical to charts/jh-3-contributions.png (cmp). Notes, not defects: (1) The note cites Pasal 28, but the ceiling is in Pasal 29. The ceiling sentence carries no citation of its own, so nothing is miscited, and adding 'Pasal 29' would be a new attribution, which the rules bar. The post's reference list cites PP 45/2015 (Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015a) for the same ceiling at draft .md:13. (2) The note and alt text name a ceiling for JP but not for CPF, whose Ordinary Wage ceiling is not in any stored source (round 1 said so). A reader may infer that CPF has none. Nothing stated is false under the rate wording, and the owner settled this point after round 6 H2. Any fix would need a new number or source, so I do not refute it. LOW, for the owner's awareness only. | L: The MDX:79-83 figcaption equals the inventory text after whitespace normalisation (script: True), and it equals make_charts.py:171-177 shown in the PNG. Clauses: (1) 'the rates the regulations set (PP 46/2015 Pasal 16; PP 45/2015 Pasal 28)' is supported by pp_46_2015.txt:428-434 (5.7% = 2 + 3.7) and pp_45_2015.txt:820-832 (3% = 2 + 1). (2) The 401(k) clause is supported by HAS highlights :224 (12.1% in 2024) and the average deferral of 7.6% in 2024 (sources.json has_average_deferral). Both exclude non-contributors (HAS :2563-2566), so 'among participants' and 'a difference of two averages' are accurate (4.5 = 12.1 - 7.6). (3) 'CPF Board contribution rates in force on 1 January 2026 for wages in the top band, the same for each age group up to 55' is supported by the CSV 2026-01 rows (37 for all four groups up to 55) and the metadata ('highest wage band'). (4) 'JP is a separate pension scheme, and its rate applies to wages up to a ceiling' is supported by PP 45 Pasal 29(1)-(3) (pp_45_2015.txt:853-864). Not an error: the article parenthetical sits on the rates sentence and names only Pasal 28, while the ceiling is in Pasal 29, which the note does not name. A reader checking Pasal 28 will not find the ceiling there, but no clause is wrong, and naming Pasal 29 would be an addition that the fix rules do not allow. | K: With whitespace normalised, the MDX:79-83 figcaption is identical to the footnote string at make_charts.py:171-177 with year=2024 and max_age=55 (lens-K/cmp_caption.py printed 'caption==note: True'). The note rendered in the opened PNG has the same wording. Support: 'The rates the regulations set' is backed by PP 46/2015 Pasal 16(1) (pp_46_2015.txt:426-434: '5,7% ... dari Upah', 2% worker, 3.7% employer) and PP 45/2015 Pasal 28(2) (pp_45_2015.txt:824-825: '3% ... dari Upah per bulan'). 'In force on 1 January 2026' and 'up to 55' match results.json cpf in_force '2026-01', the four age groups and max_age 55. 'JP ... its rate applies to wages up to a ceiling' is backed by Pasal 29(2) (pp_45_2015.txt:855), which is in the regulation the note cites. Minor (LOW, not wrong): the pinpoint in the note names Pasal 28 only, while the ceiling is in Pasal 29.
